issues.description: The solution for Aufgabe 02 uses an incorrect join column: it matches Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.id (solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql lines 3), but the problem schema and other solutions use the pattern of a foreign key named gemeindeschluessel on the place-specific tables (e.g. Schwimmbad.gemeindeschluessel in other solutions). Using Freizeitpark.id as the join column is inconsistent with the intended schema and with how joins are written elsewhere, and will produce wrong results or confuse students about the correct foreign-key column to use.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the join in solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql to use the municipality foreign-key column on Freizeitpark. For example: WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel. Ensure the template and solution consistently use Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel as the foreign-key column so students are not misled about the schema.

issues.description: The Freizeitpark table is joined to Gemeinde using the column Freizeitpark.id in solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql, while other entity tables (Zoo, Schwimmbad, Radweg_zu_Gemeinde, etc.) consistently use a gemeindeschluessel column (e.g. Zoo.gemeindeschluessel, Schwimmbad.gemeindeschluessel) to link to Gemeinde.schluessel. This inconsistent identifier (id vs. gemeindeschluessel) for the same conceptual foreign-key relationship can confuse students about which column represents the municipality key and which column to use for joins.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a consistent foreign-key column name for Freizeitpark to match the schema convention used elsewhere. Replace Freizeitpark.id with Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel in the join condition. Example correction for solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql: WHERE Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel
